# bunway

> A self-hosted LLM gateway on Bun: one container, zero runtime dependencies,
> OpenAI-compatible API, priority failover, SQLite billing, built-in console.
> Contracts in this file are an index; the source is authoritative.

Read `AGENTS.md` for repo layout and dev commands.

## Source of truth

| Fact | File |
|---|---|
| Admin API (paths, payloads, validation, status codes) | `apps/gateway/src/admin.ts` |
| DB schema and record fields | `apps/gateway/src/db.ts` |
| Routing order, cooldown, error classification | `apps/gateway/src/router.ts` |
| Pricing rules, cost math, usage normalization | `apps/gateway/src/billing.ts` |
| Upstream dialects (chat / messages / responses) | `apps/gateway/src/dialect.ts` |
| Startup env vars and defaults | `apps/gateway/src/index.ts` (`main`) |
| Deploy compose files | `demo/`, `deploy/` |

## Task 1 — deploy

Zero-key demo (mock upstream, pre-seeded data, console filled):

```bash
docker compose -f demo/docker-compose.yml up -d
bash demo/smoke.sh http://127.0.0.1:3101 demo-admin-token sk-demo
```

Console: http://127.0.0.1:3101/console, token `demo-admin-token`. The demo binds
`127.0.0.1` only; `docker compose -f demo/docker-compose.yml down -v` removes it.

Production (real upstreams, single container):

```bash
printf 'GATEWAY_ADMIN_TOKEN=%s\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > deploy/.env
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.service.yml up -d --build
bash demo/smoke.sh http://127.0.0.1:3001 <that-admin-token> <client-key>
```

Env vars an agent must set: `ADMIN_TOKEN` (required, process exits without it),
`PORT` (3001), `DB_PATH` (/data/gateway.db in the image), `STATIC_DIR`
(/app/static in the image), `LOG_DIR` (/data/logs). Defaults: `index.ts` + `tester.ts`.

Done when: `demo/smoke.sh` exits 0.

## Task 2 — configure an upstream provider

```bash
curl -s http://<host>:3001/admin/providers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"my-upstream","base_url":"https://api.deepseek.com","api_key":"sk-...",
       "routes":[{"gateway_model":"fast","provider_model":"deepseek-chat","priority":10,
                  "api":["chat"],
                  "pricing":{"default":{"price_input":0.15,"price_output":0.6,
                                        "price_cache_read":0.003,"price_cache_write":0}}}]}'
```

- `base_url` is the host root **without** `/v1` (the gateway appends
  `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` or `/v1/responses` per route `api`).
- `api_key` is write-only: `GET /admin/providers` never returns it. To rotate,
  `PUT /admin/providers/<id>` with the full object including the new key.
- Optional `meta`: `extra_headers` (static), `forward_headers` (copy named
  headers from the client request; never list `authorization`/`x-api-key`),
  `requires_reasoning_content`.
- Pricing is USD per million tokens.

Done when: `GET /admin/providers` lists it and a chat request reaches it.

## Task 3 — configure gateway routes

A route connects `gateway_model` (what clients ask for) to
`provider_model` (what the upstream gets) on one provider.

```bash
curl -s http://<host>:3001/admin/routes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"gateway_model":"fast","provider_id":1,"provider_model":"deepseek-chat",
       "priority":10,"api":["chat","responses"],
       "pricing":{"default":{"price_input":0.15,"price_output":0.6,
                             "price_cache_read":0.003,"price_cache_write":0}}}'
```

- Several routes with the same `gateway_model` = a failover group; higher
  `priority` is tried first unless `dynamic_priority` is on.
- `api` lists the dialects the upstream speaks; `/v1/responses` only routes to
  routes declaring `responses`.
- `pricing.rules` adds UTC time windows (`"windows":["12:00-18:00"]`,
  `days:[1,2,3,4,5]`) for peak/off-peak prices.
- List: `GET /admin/routes`. Update in place: `PUT /admin/routes?gateway_model=&provider_id=&provider_model=`.

Done when: `GET /v1/models` (client key) includes the `gateway_model` and a chat
request returns 200.

## Task 4 — point a client or coding agent at it

```bash
curl -s http://<host>:3001/admin/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"my-agent","key":"sk-mine"}'
```

Any OpenAI-compatible client: `base_url = http://<host>:3001/v1`,
`api_key = <client key>`, `api = chat completions`.

Pi (`~/.pi/agent/models.json`) keeps the same shape as any OpenAI provider:

```json
{"providers":{"bunway":{"baseUrl":"http://HOST:3001/v1","apiKey":"sk-mine",
  "api":"openai-completions","compat":{"supportsDeveloperRole":false},
  "models":[{"id":"fast","name":"Fast","cost":{"input":0.15,"output":0.6,"cacheRead":0.003,"cacheWrite":0}}]}}}
```

`/v1/responses` works only stateless (`store:true` and `previous_response_id`
are rejected); see `docs/agents.md` for the full recipes.

Done when: the client gets a streamed answer and `/admin/stats` shows the request.

## Hard constraints

- `/admin/*` and `/console` are token-gated but the console HTML is served
  without auth; keep the port on a trusted network.
- The gateway has zero npm runtime dependencies — `bun run src/index.ts` is the
  whole dev loop; there is nothing to `npm install` for the gateway.
- Never edit the SQLite file directly; providers/routes/keys go through the
  admin API.
